title: device-telemetry-sampler-v0-sketch
content:
Notes (scratch) — device-telemetry-sampler v0

Context:
- Goal: a small, client-side sampler for mobile/edge apps that reduces telemetry upload cost while keeping high-fidelity signals for regressions and SLOs.
- Motivation: token-level telemetry from mobile clients is noisy and expensive; we want bounded bandwidth and predictable cost with tunable fidelity.
- Audience: SDK owners (mobile + JS), product analytics, infra (ingest/gateway), SRE for alerting.

Constraints & principles:
1) deterministic-ish: sampling config should allow reproducible sampling for a session id + seed so we can re-simulate cadence in testing.
2) privacy first: no raw PII; enable local redaction and opt-out.
3) graceful degradation: if network constrained, fall back to extremely sparse summaries.
4) low CPU/memory on client (mobile).
5) controllable remotely: feature flag + config + rollout.

High-level sketch (ASCII):

  [Client App]
       | events/token-metrics (streamed)
       v
  [Telemetry Sampler] -- sampled payloads --> [Local Buffer] --> [Upload Gateway] --> [Ingest]
       |
       +-- local counters/aggregates (for immediate UI diagnostics)

Core components (client-side):
- Sampler module (deterministic sampling decision per event)
- Aggregator (windowed summaries, histograms, percentiles)
- Upload manager (batching, backoff, fallback policy)
- Config/feature-flag hook (remote config + local overrides)

Proposed API surface (SDK):
- Telemetry.addEvent(eventType: string, payload: object) -> returns void
- Telemetry.startSession(sessionId: string, opts?)
- Telemetry.flush(sync=false)
- Telemetry.configure({ samplingConfigUrl, maxBytesPerHour, allowPII })

HTTP/ingest shape (minimal example)
POST /v1/client-telemetry HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <device-key-or-token>

{
  "session_id": "s_1234",
  "client_id": "c_abc",
  "sampled_at": "2025-02-20T15:02:00Z",
  "events": [
    {"t":"inference.request","seq":412,"tokens":34,"lat_ms":120},
    {"t":"model.fallback","seq":413,"reason":"no-capacity"}
  ],
  "aggregates": {"p50_lat_ms":"110","p95_lat_ms":"210","tokens_sum":"12345"}
}

Config schema (proposal, remote YAML delivered by FF):
----
# sampler-config v1
global:
  max_bytes_per_hour: 51200        # bytes per device per hour
  default_strategy: "stratified"
strategies:
  - name: "sparse"
    target_rate: 0.02              # 2% of events
    stratify_by: ["event_type"]
  - name: "stratified"
    strata:
      - by: "event_type"
        rates: {"inference.request": 0.05, "model.error": 1.0}
  - name: "adaptive"
    init_rate: 0.05
    increase_on_error: 2.0
----

Sampling strategies (short):
- uniform: random keep with probability p
- stratified: keep with per-event-type rates (cheap and effective)
- deterministic-hash: hash(session_id + event_seq) % 1 < p (replayable)
- adaptive: start with baseline, increase sampling for anomalous signal (errors, regressions) or when server requests higher fidelity (on-demand replay)

Pseudocode (deterministic-hash sampler):
function keepEvent(sessionId, seq, p) {
  key = sessionId + ":" + seq
  h = murmur64(key) / MAX_UINT64
  return h < p
}

Local aggregation windows:
- sliding 60s window for latency buckets (p50/p95)
- 10m summary window for token distribution
- daily counters for quota enforcement

Upload/backoff rules:
- batch threshold: N events or T seconds (e.g., 50 events or 30s)
- if connection metered or on cellular (user opt-in policy) reduce to min_rate
- if buffer > max_bytes_per_hour, enable coarse summaries only (counts + histograms)

Server-side hints & on-demand mode:
- server can request sampling upgrades per client via push/longpoll or next-response header ("X-Telemetry-Rate: uplift=3x for 5m").
- server will accept replay tokens to retrieve dense logs from device (opt-in, encrypted), used sparingly for debugging.

Telemetry payload examples (sparse vs dense):
- sparse: only event metadata + small stats
- dense: full token-level traces (only allowed for opted-in internal builds)

Privacy considerations:
- default: no raw prompt text or PII in telemetry. Hash or redact text fields on device.
- explicit opt-in flow for verbose traces (developer/dev build) with clear TTL and upload controls.
- per-country rate limits and retention enforcement; config flags to disable uploads (e.g., GDPR opt-out).

Operational metrics to expose:
- bytes/hour per device distribution
- sampling rate achieved vs target (by event type)
- latencies of telemetry ingestion pipeline
- error rate of telemetry uploads (client throttling/backoff)

Rollout plan (sketch):
1) internal dogfood in SDK canary (nightly) build with detailed logs disabled by default but sampling enabled at low rate.
2) measure cost and signal for 2 weeks, iterate on stratified rates.
3) expose FF to 10% of users with uplift for specific customer segments.
4) GA with telemetry dashboard and SLOs for telemetry pipeline.

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle cross-device sessions (same user across multiple devices) and deduplication?
- Are device-side keys acceptable for per-device identity or do we need ephemeral session tokens?
- Risk of skew: sampling can hide rare but important failures. Need on-demand upgrade flow.
- SDK upgrades on old app versions (fallback behavior needed).

Next steps (me / short checklist):
- [ ] prototype deterministic-hash sampler in mobile-android SDK (Samir)
- [ ] add config fetch + local validation (Lina)
- [ ] mock ingest endpoint in dev infra and run cost simulation with synthetic traces
- [ ] document privacy/PIA checklist and work with legal

References & notes:
- related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/432 (ingest changes)
- jira: JIRA-INF-1284 (telemetry cost cap epic)
- slack thread: #eng-telemetry (see pinned examples)

Random ideas to keep if time: local differential privacy for counts, exporting small histograms only, and a desktop dev-mode agent that can temporarily flip sampling to 100% for debugging.

End of scratch.
